key_insight: Particle shape controls collective Marangoni surfing: prolate ellipses tend to attract, while oblate ellipses tend to repel, influencing the stability of polarized populations.
engineering_relevance: The formulation offers a computationally tractable route to modeling and potentially designing shape-controlled, surfactant-driven particle assemblies at fluid interfaces.
method: Assume low Reynolds and Péclet numbers.
Reduce nonlocal surface–bulk coupling to integral equations on particles and their boundaries.
Use custom spectral simulations and a far-field reduced-order model.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations reveal shape-sensitive collective dynamics, with attraction and repulsion trends rationalized by a far-field expansion.
watch_item: Applicability beyond low Reynolds and Péclet numbers is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: A boundary integral formulation for microscale Marangoni surfing
